titleEn: Women who changed science missing from GCSE and A-level courses – new study
titleZh: 新研究：改变科学的女性，仍在中学科学课程中缺席
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: Cast your mind back to your secondary school science classroom: the fiery glow of Bunsen burners, scratched safety goggles that never quite fit, and a giant periodic table pinned to the wall.
paragraphs.zh: 把你的思绪抛回到你的中学科学教室：本生灯的炽热光芒，刮伤的护目镜，从来没有完全适合，和一个巨大的周期表钉在墙上。

paragraphs.en: When you learned about the breakthroughs that shaped our world and the people who made them, whose names were attached? From Newton’s laws to Darwin’s theory of natural selection, the ones you remember are almost certainly male.
paragraphs.zh: 当你了解到塑造我们世界的重大突破以及做出这些突破的人时，你会发现，从牛顿定律到达尔文的自然选择理论，你能记住的几乎都是男性。

paragraphs.en: That experience was not just down to individual teachers. It was and still is written into official GCSE and A-level course specifications. Because these early stages form the foundation of our science education, their omissions stick with us for life.
paragraphs.zh: 这种经验不仅仅是个别教师的经验。它过去是，现在仍然是写在官方的GCSE和A级课程说明书中。因为这些早期阶段构成了我们科学教育的基础，它们的遗漏将伴随我们一生。

paragraphs.en: Half of the British population can’t name one woman scientist. Leaving women out of national specifications sends an implicit message about who science is really for.
paragraphs.zh: 一半的英国人连一个女科学家的名字都叫不出来。把女性排除在国家标准之外，这就隐含了一个信息，那就是科学到底是为谁服务的。

paragraphs.en: In our new study, led by researchers at the University of Cambridge alongside IncludeHer, a collaborative project working to improve the representation of women in school science education, we analysed over 40 science specifications: the knowledge required to pass exams. We examined the specifications for six main exam boards for Key Stage 4 (GCSEs) and Key Stage 5 (A-levels), and for Scotland’s National 5s and Highers.
paragraphs.zh: 在我们的新研究中，由剑桥大学的研究人员和IncludeHer（一个致力于提高女性在学校科学教育中的代表性的合作项目）领导，我们分析了40多个科学规范：通过考试所需的知识。我们检查了关键阶段4（GCSE）和关键阶段5（A-levels）的六个主要考试委员会的规范，以及苏格兰国家5s和更高的考试。

paragraphs.en: Our work builds on an earlier Australian study led by astrophysicist Dr Kat Ross, which uncovered a striking lack of female scientists in high school curricula. We set out to investigate whether UK specifications have similar omissions.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的工作建立在天体物理学家Kat Ross博士领导的澳大利亚早期研究的基础上，该研究发现高中课程中女性科学家的数量明显不足。我们着手调查英国的规范是否也有类似的遗漏。

paragraphs.en: Across 224 unique scientists referenced in UK specifications, discoveries are taught almost exclusively through concepts named after men, with only three mentioning women in total.
paragraphs.zh: 在英国规范中引用的224位独特的科学家中，发现几乎完全通过以男性命名的概念来教授，只有三位提到女性。

paragraphs.en: Inge Lehmann, who discovered that the Earth has a solid inner core surrounded by a liquid outer core, is cited in A-level Geology via the “Lehmann discontinuity”.
paragraphs.zh: Inge Lehmann发现了地球有一个被液体外核包围的固体内核，他通过“Lehmann不连续性”在A级地质学中被引用。

paragraphs.en: Marie Tharp, who mapped the ocean floor and identified the Mid-Atlantic Ridge rift valley, is also mentioned in A-level geology. She provided vital evidence for continental drift, despite being prohibited from boarding research vessels for years and having her ideas dismissed as “girl talk”.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽·萨普绘制了海底地图，并确定了大西洋中脊裂谷，她也在A级地质学中被提及。尽管多年来被禁止登上研究船，她的想法也被斥为“女孩的谈话”，但她为大陆漂移提供了重要证据。

paragraphs.en: Finally, Rosalind Franklin is included in two biology specifications for her X-ray crystallography work revealing the double-helix structure of DNA. Her essential data was used without attribution during her lifetime.
paragraphs.zh: 最后，罗莎琳德富兰克林因其揭示DNA双螺旋结构的X射线晶体学工作而被列入两个生物学规范，她的基本数据在她一生中被使用而没有归属。

paragraphs.en: At GCSE level, when science is compulsory for all students, Franklin is the only woman mentioned. At A-level, Lehmann and Tharp appear solely in geology, a subject taken by less than 2% of science students.
paragraphs.zh: 在普通中等教育证书（GCSE）中，理科是所有学生的必修课，富兰克林是唯一被提及的女性。在A级考试中，莱曼和萨普只出现在地质学中，而地质学是一门只有不到2%的理科学生选修的学科。

paragraphs.en: For centuries, social, economic, and institutional barriers limited women’s formal participation in science. Despite this, women made numerous key breakthroughs, and these are already taught to UK 14–18-year-olds. But the names of the women behind them did not make it onto the page.
paragraphs.zh: 几个世纪以来，社会、经济和制度障碍限制了女性对科学的正式参与。尽管如此，女性还是取得了许多关键性的突破，这些突破已经被教授给英国14-18岁的学生。但这些突破背后的女性名字并没有出现在页面上。

paragraphs.en: Why representation matters
paragraphs.zh: 为什么代表性很重要

paragraphs.en: Diversity within scientific fields drives creativity and innovation, benefiting all of society. Yet women remain underrepresented. They make up only around one third of the global scientific community, with similar figures seen within the UK workforce.
paragraphs.zh: 科学领域的多样性推动了创造力和创新，使全社会受益。然而，女性的代表性仍然不足。她们仅占全球科学界的三分之一左右，英国劳动力中也有类似的数字。

paragraphs.en: This disparity starts early on in schools: although science uptake is balanced at Key Stage 4, just two years later at Key Stage 5, physics, mathematics and further mathematics only see participation from girls at 24.1%, 37.3% and 26.9% respectively in 2025. This imbalance continues into university, where women make up roughly 25% of physics undergraduate students in the UK.
paragraphs.zh: 这种不平衡从学校的早期就开始了：虽然科学的吸收在关键阶段4是平衡的，但仅仅两年后在关键阶段5，物理，数学和进一步的数学在2025年只有24.1%，37.3%和26.9%的女孩参与。这种不平衡继续到大学，在英国，女性约占物理本科生的25%。

paragraphs.en: Introducing relatable female role models into the classroom directly boosts girls’ confidence and fosters positive attitudes towards scientific careers. But because specifications dictate mandatory exam content, teachers currently have to go out of their way to add female figures on top of busy workloads. By making small, targeted changes directly to national specifications, we can make inclusion standard practice across all schools.
paragraphs.zh: 将相关的女性榜样引入课堂直接增强了女孩的信心，培养了对科学事业的积极态度。但由于规定了强制性的考试内容，教师目前不得不在忙碌的工作之外特意增加女性人物。通过直接针对国家规定进行小而有针对性的改变，我们可以在所有学校实现包容性标准实践。

paragraphs.en: We propose inserting one female scientist per subject into topics that are already compulsory, but where the woman’s name is missing.
paragraphs.zh: 我们建议在已经是必修课但没有女性名字的科目中，每科增加一名女性科学家。

paragraphs.en: This means introducing Marie Skłodowska-Curie, who coined the term radioactivity and discovered polonium and radium, when teaching atomic structure and radioactivity, and Lise Meitner, who provided the first theoretical explanation of nuclear fission, when discussing this concept. GCSE astronomy should include Jocelyn Bell Burnell, who discovered pulsars: rotating neutron stars used as cosmic clocks.
paragraphs.zh: 这意味着在教授原子结构和放射性时，要介绍创造了放射性这个术语并发现了钋和镭的玛丽·斯克洛多夫斯卡-居里，在讨论这个概念时，要介绍第一个对核裂变进行理论解释的莉泽·迈特纳。

paragraphs.en: Biology teaching can include Dorothy Hodgkin on protein structure, the only British female Nobel laureate in science, and Tu Youyou, a Nobel laureate whose work led to the development of an antimalarial drug.
paragraphs.zh: 生物学教学可以包括多萝西·霍奇金（Dorothy Hodgkin）的蛋白质结构，她是唯一的英国女性诺贝尔科学奖获得者，屠呦呦是诺贝尔奖获得者，她的工作导致了抗疟疾药物的开发。

paragraphs.en: In chemistry, schools can teach about Stephanie Kwolek, the inventor of Kevlar, when covering polymers. For physics, they can include Annie Jump Cannon when describing the classification of stars. And in environmental science, classes can discuss the pivotal work of Susan Solomon for understanding Antarctic ozone depletion.
paragraphs.zh: 在化学课上，学校可以在讲授聚合物时介绍凯夫拉纤维的发明者斯蒂芬妮·克沃莱克（Stephanie Kwolek）;在物理课上，可以在介绍恒星分类时介绍安妮·坎农（Annie Jump Cannon）;在环境科学课上，可以讨论苏珊·所罗门（Susan Solomon）为理解南极臭氧层损耗所做的关键工作。

paragraphs.en: By making these simple additions to science specifications, we can change the message we send to the next generation. Whoever they are, every student sitting in a classroom deserves to know that the story of science belongs to them too.
paragraphs.zh: 通过对科学规范做这些简单的补充，我们可以改变我们传递给下一代的信息。无论他们是谁，坐在教室里的每一个学生都应该知道，科学的故事也属于他们。
